title: A live HTML mockup of the new Watch the run: overlay that grows into a full-screen session
name: session-mock
description:
Design first, code second. Build one self-contained HTML page that replays a fake run on a timer and shows the whole target design, then publish it as an artifact for the user to review.

Must show:
- Opens as the wide overlay (today's 980px, `apps/dashboard/src/logs/Logs.tsx`). A full-screen button (and `f`) grows it into a full-screen terminal-like session with an animated transition (FLIP / View Transitions; shrink back the same way). `prefers-reduced-motion` gets a crossfade.
- Full-screen layout: title bar (`sober › <node name>`, host · model), transcript, answer prompt, status bar (running dot, elapsed, tool count, checks n/m).
- Transcript in Claude Code idiom: `⏺` agent text lines (no boxes), `⏺ Read(path)` tool blocks with `⎿` result summary, long output folded behind a click, `✻ Thinking… (12s)` spinner with rotating verb, `N new lines ↓` pill when scrolled up, acceptance checks turning into a ✓/✗ checklist card at the end.
- Keyboard: f, Esc, j/k, g/G, /.
- Dark and light, OKLCH tokens only, taken from `apps/dashboard/src/theme.css`. Propose the narrow transcript palette the ADR in transcript-adr will record.
- Show two font options side by side (the system mono stack in theme.css vs JetBrains Mono + IBM Plex Sans) so the user can pick.

What a line can show depends on the line-shape decision: mock what that answer makes available. Commit the page to `docs/design/watch-the-run.html`. No product code changes.

brief.approach:
Build one self-contained page, `docs/design/watch-the-run.html`: inline CSS and inline JS, no build step, no product code touched. It is the design the implementation nodes (transcript-adr, session-shell, tool-blocks, session-statusbar) will copy, so it must look like the real dashboard. It must not look like a generic landing page.

1. Tokens. Copy the semantic tokens from `apps/dashboard/src/theme.css` as-is: `--bg --surface --raised --line --line-soft --ink --ink-dim --ink-faint --danger --status-*`, the radii, and the text scale 11–24px. Keep both themes: dark by default, light under `prefers-color-scheme`, and a `data-theme` toggle button in the page corner. Use OKLCH only, never hex. Add a small block of proposed transcript tokens: `--tx-tool --tx-result --tx-error --tx-think --tx-human`, in dark and light. Pick hues that stay clear of the five status colours and `--danger`. Label the block "proposed for ADR 0064". ADR 0039 still reserves colour for status everywhere outside the transcript.

2. Scripted replay. A JS array of fake `LogLine`s in the enriched shape the line-shape decision chose (`enrich-line`). Each line has `kind`, `text` and `tool`, plus the new fields the transcript needs: an argument summary (`Read(apps/dashboard/src/logs/data.ts)`), a result summary line (`92 lines`, `+14 −6`, `exit 0`) and a timestamp. A timer appends the lines one by one at realistic gaps. The whole run takes about 40 s. A Replay button restarts it.

3. The frame. The page opens with a canvas-like dimmed backdrop and the wide overlay (980px, like `Logs.tsx` today). A full-screen button in the header, and the `f` key, grow the overlay into a full-screen session with a FLIP transform/opacity animation of about 280 ms on an ease-out curve. Shrinking back mirrors it and is a little faster. Under `prefers-reduced-motion` it becomes a 120 ms crossfade. The full-screen frame has these parts:
   - A title bar: three muted window dots, `sober › session-mock` and a right-aligned `claude · opus`.
   - The transcript.
   - The answer prompt, as a `>` line textarea.
   - A status bar: a pulsing running dot, elapsed mm:ss, a `⚒ N tools` counter and `◌ n/m checks`.

4. The transcript, in Claude Code idiom:
   - Agent text is a `⏺` line in sans ink, with no box. Tool calls are `⏺ Read(path)` in mono, followed by an indented `⎿` result in dim ink.
   - Output longer than 4 lines folds to 3 lines plus a `… +N lines (click to expand)` row.
   - `raw` stderr uses `--tx-error`. A human answer uses a `›` mark in `--tx-human`.
   - While the agent is working, the last row is `✻ Thinking… (12s)`: a spinner glyph that rotates through ✻✳✢· and a verb that changes every few seconds. The spinner freezes into a static line when the next line lands.
   - At the end, the `check`/`checked` lines collapse into a checklist card with ✓/✗ per acceptance entry, and the status bar reads "ended".
   - Keep `aria-live="polite"` on the status bar only.

5. Following. Auto-follow works only while the reader is at the bottom, using the same 24px slack as `atBottom` in `logs/data.ts`. When the reader scrolls up, a floating `N new lines ↓` pill appears. Clicking it jumps back to the bottom.

6. Keyboard: `f` toggles full screen. `Esc` leaves full screen first, then closes. `j`/`k` scroll. `g`/`G` go to top/bottom. `/` opens a find box that filters the lines. Keys are ignored while the textarea has focus. Focus rings stay visible.

7. Font comparison. A small segmented switch in the corner, "System mono" / "JetBrains Mono + IBM Plex Sans", swaps the transcript's font. The two web fonts load from Google Fonts only. Label the switch clearly so the user can pick one.

Add a short HTML comment at the top that says what the page is and that nothing in it is product code. After the run, the reviewer publishes the file as an artifact for the user.

acceptance.proves: the mockup exists at the path the later nodes will read
no product code changed; the node is design only

acceptance.run: for s in '⏺' '⎿' '✻' 'new lines' 'prefers-reduced-motion' 'JetBrains Mono' 'data-theme' 'aria-live' '--tx-tool' '--status-running'; do grep -qF -- "$s" docs/design/watch-the-run.html || { echo "missing: $s"; exit 1; }; done
acceptance.proves: every required piece is on the page: transcript idiom, spinner, jump pill, reduced motion, font comparison, both themes, live status bar, proposed transcript tokens, the dashboard's own status tokens
colours are OKLCH like theme.css, no hex slipped in
the page is self-contained: no external script
